newsitem.title: INDIA: India defers sugar exports deregulation bill.
newsitem.headline: India defers sugar exports deregulation bill.

text.p: India's upper house on Friday deferred approval of a bill seeking to end the monopoly of a private trading agency over sugar exports, the Press Trust of India (PTI) reported.
PTI said the bill, seeking to repeal the Sugar Export Promotion Act, 1958, was deferred after senior deputies in the upper house asked the government not to rush the legislation through.
On Thursday, the Indian parliament's lower house approved the bill, aimed at deregulating exports.
The bill needs to be approved by the upper house before being submitted for presidential assent.
Parliament ended its winter session on Friday and is scheduled to reassemble only in February.

Indian sugar exports are currently channelled through the Indian Sugar and General Industries Export-Import Corp (ISGIEC), an agency set up by private millers. It is the only body permitted to export sugar.
The bill would permit private firms registered with the Agriculture and Processed Foods Export Development Association (APEDA) to export sugar.
Indian Food Minister Devendra Prasd Yadav said on Thursday the measure would ensure the production of good quality sugar and end the present monopoly of a single trading agency.
